solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Quote about a politician's temporary home?

indicators.note: placed around, so the quoting word is wrapped round what follows

parts.note: to quote a source is to cite it
an MP is a Member of Parliament; the possessive gives MP'S

explanation.surface: Someone quoting a remark about where a politician lives for now.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitch for a tent or caravan is a place one lives in only briefly, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Get firm with legally incompetent person who lacks guts?

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a ward is someone placed under a guardian because they cannot manage their legal affairs

explanation.surface: Acquiring a business with someone legally unfit, a gutless move.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking guts means lacking courage, which describes a spineless person.

clue.text: Dine at home in place for meals — what's the quality of the beef?

indicators.note: placed inside, so eating at home goes within the dining hall

parts.note: a mess is where military personnel eat
to dine is to eat
in means at home

explanation.surface: Eating in the canteen and asking how good the beef is.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef rated for how much substantial flesh it has; the question mark allows the figurative sense of substance too.

clue.text: Unhappy about the message of defiance

indicators.note: around, so the word for unhappy goes round the next word

parts.note: sore means aggrieved or unhappy

explanation.surface: Someone upset at a defiant message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is not a link word here: it is the inner piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A childish retort of defiance used to have the last word.

clue.text: Middle of letter conveys little that folk today might want to read

definitions.text: that folk today might want to read

indicators.note: carries within, so the central pair holds the small word
the two central letters of the word letter are taken

parts.note: wee means little

explanation.surface: A short note in a letter that modern people would read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' is six letters, so its middle is the central pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A short social media post is a modern form of reading matter, which people now look at instead of letters.

clue.text: Trails back to a heavenly dwelling-place

indicators.note: read in the opposite direction, so the word for trails is written right to left

parts.note: to trail something along is to drag it

explanation.surface: Paths leading back to a paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reads the trails word right to left; 'to' merely joins it to 'a', which comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology this is the realm of the gods, a celestial home.

clue.text: Escorted queen entertained by father and daughter

indicators.note: hosted by, so the queen goes inside the father

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father
D is short for daughter, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A queen accompanied while being hosted by a father and daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To accompany a lady as her attendant was to act as her squire.

clue.text: Woman giving a sign that character must be got rid of?

parts.words: sign that character must be got rid of?
parts.note: dele is the proofreader's mark telling the printer to delete a character

explanation.surface: A woman gesturing that someone's personality must be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' here is a printed letter, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is a woman's name, famously the British singer.

clue.text: Before half-term it's sad to stir up negative feeling

indicators.note: stirring mixes things around, so these letters are rearranged
the first two of the four letters of term are used

explanation.surface: Sad to cause bad feeling just before a school's mid-term break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir up' makes DISTAS from it's sad; 'Before' places it ahead of the half of term.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is dislike or aversion, an unfavourable reaction.

clue.text: In extremis teacher gets hostile and cross

indicators.note: taken at its extremes, so only the first and last letters of teacher are used

parts.note: averse means opposed or hostile

explanation.surface: A teacher at breaking point becomes hostile and angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In extremis' normally means in dire straits; here it takes T and R from teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to cross over or travel across.

clue.text: Thus a wee terror's 'contrived to be dominant

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially arranged, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A small horror of a child scheming to rule the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' rearranges all fifteen letters of THUS A WEE TERRORS.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being the one in charge in a household or relationship.

clue.text: Object, having to wear torn clothing

indicators.note: the object goes inside the word for torn, as a body sits inside garments it wears

parts.note: rent is an old past participle of rend, meaning torn
an aim is an objective or object

explanation.surface: Someone protesting at being made to wear ripped garments.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary or archaic word for garments and dress.

clue.text: Plant woman discovered crossing mountain

indicators.note: the woman's name spans the mountain, so it is placed around it

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name
Ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

explanation.surface: A botanist finds a plant on a woman's mountain crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus of flowering garden plants, also called vervain.

clue.text: One who switches sides failing other soldiers

parts.note: a failing is a flaw or defect
OR stands for Other Ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A turncoat let down by the troops around him.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserter who abandons one side or country for the opposing one.

clue.text: Sliding vehicle to advance, when one gets out, across marsh

indicators.note: spanning, so the outer words go either side of the marsh
this word says some letters are taken away from the word it governs
the letter for one leaves the word for advance

parts.note: to gain is to advance or progress
I is the Roman numeral for one
a bog is a marsh

explanation.surface: A sled used to push forward over swampy ground after someone climbs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when one gets out' drops the Roman one from the advance word; 'across' sets the marsh between the two outer parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow sled for sliding down snowy slopes.

clue.text: Leading journalist back in HQ?

indicators.note: the whole phrase is read in reverse order

parts.note: top means leading or foremost
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A senior reporter returning to the newspaper's head office.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a central base or store, which the question mark admits is a loose fit for headquarters.

clue.text: Get into author's English, special treat

parts.note: a pen stands for an author, as in a pen for hire

indicators.note: made special, so treat is turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Getting hold of a writer's English, a particular treat.
explanation.definitionFit: To penetrate is to enter or pierce something.

clue.text: Member of the House given binder — first one is wrong

indicators.note: the numeral for one is placed at the front

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP, a Member of Parliament, sits in the House of Commons
a roper is one who ties with rope, a binder

explanation.surface: An MP is given a ring binder and the first one is incorrect.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper means incorrect or unsuitable.

clue.text: Craftsman depicting Mary and Jesus?

parts.note: Mary is the mother of Jesus, so she is MA
Jesus is the Son, in Christian terms

explanation.surface: An artisan making an image of the Virgin and Child.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary and Jesus are a mother and her son.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoneworker, a skilled tradesman who cuts and lays stone.

clue.text: Numbers besieging one East- End dwelling may be offensive

indicators.note: surrounding, so the numbers abbreviation goes around the one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
in a Cockney accent of London's East End the H is dropped, so home becomes 'OME

explanation.surface: Crowds around a Cockney home might be unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means foul-smelling, disgusting or harmful.

clue.text: Female ending bedecked in jewellery is given approval

indicators.note: covered in ornaments, so the suffix sits inside the word for jewellery

parts.note: bling is slang for showy jewellery
-ess is a suffix making a feminine noun, as in lioness

explanation.surface: A woman's finale, dripping with jewels, wins acclaim.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving one's blessing to a plan means sanctioning or endorsing it.

clue.text: One sounding drunk may be lying on the beach

definitions.text: may be lying on the beach

indicators.note: a slurred speaker turns the S sound to SH

parts.note: single means one

explanation.surface: A tipsy person sprawled on the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: SINGLE said with a drunken slur.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is the mass of small pebbles covering many British beaches.

clue.text: Home worker, female having to stay in for me?

definitions.text: Home worker, female having to stay in for me?

indicators.note: the female letter remains inside the home and worker pair

parts.note: in means at home
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A baby asks if a mother working from home must stay in for its sake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having to stay in' puts F inside INANT. The whole clue is the baby speaking: a woman confined at home because of me.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby needs a parent to stay at home to look after it, as the speaker in the clue.

clue.text: Splendid old-fashioned dancing? No time for that!

indicators.note: this word says some letters are taken away from the word it governs
there is no room for the time letter, so it is removed from the dancing word

parts.note: tripping, as in tripping the light fantastic, means dancing

explanation.surface: Someone recalling dated dancing as splendid, but with no time for it now.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIPPING without T. The definition includes 'old-fashioned' because the word is dated slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated British slang for excellent or marvellous, much used in old schoolboy stories.

clue.text: Insistence on correctness doesn't allow for second religious holiday

indicators.note: makes no room for, so the letter is removed

parts.note: purism is strict insistence on correct usage

explanation.surface: A stickler won't make time for a second festival.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish festival commemorating the deliverance told in the Book of Esther.

clue.text: Member of family with inclination to eat cheese

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the slant goes inside the family member

parts.note: a son is a member of a family
a tilt is a slope or inclination

explanation.surface: A relative with a fondness for eating cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong blue-veined English cheese, named after a village in Cambridgeshire.

clue.text: Item of clothing is nicked

definitions.meaning: a long scarf or shawl worn round the shoulders
nicked is British slang for ..., took illegally

explanation.surface: A garment has been pinched.
explanation.definitionFit: A shawl-like wrap is one sense; the past tense of steal, meaning pinched, is the other.

clue.text: Grandma has struck arrogant pose outside -— someone to ignore

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the granny word
struck as in knocked about, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother

explanation.surface: An elderly woman striking a haughty stance, then being snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struck' rearranges ARROGANT POSE into PERSOONGRATA, and 'outside' wraps it round NAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for an unwelcome person, someone shunned or excluded.

clue.text: Stranger gets glass in the bar

definitions.meaning: more odd: rum means odd in British slang, and this is its comparative
a large drinking glass, the sort used in a pub

explanation.surface: A newcomer orders a drink in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum means peculiar, so this is more peculiar; it is also a large stemmed drinking goblet.

clue.text: Always stepping into the breach, showing great respect

indicators.note: the word for always goes inside the gap

parts.note: a rent is a tear or breach
ever means always

explanation.surface: Someone always first into the breach, earning admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Deeply respectful, especially in a devout or worshipful way.
